questions.question: Which set has cardinality $\aleph_0$?
What kind of infinity is represented by $\aleph_0$?
options: Only the size of finite sets
The size of an interval of real numbers

questions.question: When does a set have cardinality $\aleph_0$?
options: When it is a finite subset of $\mathbb N$
When it contains all real numbers
When it can be put in bijection with $\mathbb N$

questions.question: Why do $\mathbb N$, $\mathbb Z$, and $\mathbb Q$ all have the same cardinality symbol?
options: Each of them is larger than the real numbers
Each of them is an interval of real numbers
Each of them is countably infinite

questions.question: What role does a bijection play in statements about $\aleph_0$?
options: It turns every infinite set into a finite set
It proves that two sets have the same cardinality
It gives an ordering of real numbers by size
It removes the need to compare sets

questions.question: What is $\operatorname{card}(\mathbb N)$?
Which set is a standard example of cardinality $\aleph_0$?
Let $E=\{2,4,6,8,\ldots\}$. What is $\operatorname{card}(E)$?
A set can be written as $a_1,a_2,a_3,\ldots$, with every element appearing exactly once. What cardinality does the set have?
Which function is the usual evidence that the positive even numbers are countably infinite?
Why is saying “both sets are infinite” not enough to prove that both have cardinality $\aleph_0$?
options: Every infinite set is automatically finite after relabelling
No infinite set can be compared by cardinality
Cardinality applies only to subsets of $\mathbb N$
Infinite sets can have different cardinalities

questions.question: Why can $\mathbb Q$ have cardinality $\aleph_0$ even though it is dense in the real line?
options: Density is topological, while $\aleph_0$ concerns listing
Density implies a set is finite
Rational numbers are not real numbers
Every dense subset of $\mathbb R$ has cardinality $\mathfrak c$.

questions.question: What does a bijection from $\mathbb N$ to a set $A$ really provide?
options: An ordering of $A$ by numerical size
A proof that $A$ contains all real numbers.
An enumeration of $A$ with no omissions or repeats

questions.question: What is the cardinality of $\mathbb N\times\{0,1\}$?
Let $A=\{1,3,5,7,\ldots\}$. Which statement is correct?
options: $A$ is finite because it skips even numbers

questions.question: If $A$ is countably infinite and $B$ has five elements, what is the expected cardinality of $A\cup B$?
Both $\aleph_0$ and $\mathfrak{c}$ are infinite cardinals, yet $\aleph_0<\mathfrak{c}$. Which distinction explains this?
options: $\aleph_0$ is countable infinity, while $\mathfrak c$ is the cardinality of the real line
They are two notations for the same finite number
$\aleph_0$ is finite, while $\mathfrak c$ is infinite
$\aleph_0$ counts only negative integers, while $\mathfrak c$ counts only positive integers

questions.question: Why is $\aleph_0$ not contradicted by the fact that $\mathbb Z$ contains negative integers as well as positive ones?
options: Negative integers are ignored when computing cardinality.
Only positive integers are allowed in infinite sets
Cardinality depends on bijective pairing, not on looking larger

questions.question: Let $A=\{(n,0):n\in\mathbb N\}\cup\{(n,1):n\in\mathbb N\}$. What is $\operatorname{card}(A)$?
An infinite subset $S$ of $\mathbb N$ is written in increasing order as $s_1 \lt s_2 \lt s_3 \lt \cdots$. What does this show?
options: $S$ is finite because it is bounded by $\mathbb N$
